title: 60hr Tryout Lab — Hire Tryout & Mentor Script (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for a standardized 60‑hour tryout lab (contract-to-hire or short-term trial) designed for senior IC and senior+ engineering candidates. The goal: give candidates meaningful product/infra work, reduce interview bias through observable work, and provide a consistent rubric for conversion decisions.

Scope & constraints:
- Target roles: SWE (backend/frontend), ML Infra, SRE, Platform Eng. Not for exec or purely managerial hires.
- Engagement model: 60 hours (approx. 2 calendar weeks, ~7.5–8 hrs/day over 8 business days or condensed into 10 business days at 6 hrs/day).
- Employment classification: contractor with explicit trial agreement; conversion contingent on pass criteria. Legal review required per region (US/EU/APAC variations).
- Pay: standardized market-aligned hourly rate for the role band + $200 completion bonus on conversion decision (to encourage completion).

Candidate experience design (high level):
1) Pre-Start (Day -3 to Day 0)
   - Send clear orientation packet: goals, schedule, Slack channel, Confluence sandbox, sample data/keys.
   - Kickoff call (30m): People Ops + hiring manager + mentor — set expectations and check access.
   - Share deliverables doc and scoring rubric link.
2) Execution (Day 1–Day 8) 
   - Day 1: Onboarding / environment setup / quick architecture overview (mentor-led, 2–3h).
   - Days 2–6: Core tasks (candidate works asynchronously + daily 30m standup with mentor).
   - Day 7: Integration and polish (candidate pairs with mentor on final integration, 2–4h).
   - Day 8: Demo & closeout (30–45m demo + 30m feedback loop).
3) Wrap (within 48h after Day 8)
   - Hiring panel review (asynchronous scoring + 45m calibration meeting if needed).
   - Conversion decision communicated within 72h.

Sample task framing guidance (for hiring manager / hiring panel):
- Tasks should be scoped to 30–40 hours of individual work with additional 10–20 hours for integration and review.
- Prefer: one small end-to-end feature, one reliability/bug improvement, and one short design note.
- Avoid: tasks that require long-running model training, access to sensitive production data, or tasks that are ambiguous without clear acceptance criteria.

Mentor playbook (concise script / what the mentor should do):
- Before start: clone candidate repo template, provision sandbox, create a 4‑item checklist in Confluence.
- Kickoff script (30m):
   - "Welcome — quick intros. Here’s the problem space, product context, and success criteria. We’ll pair occasionally; you’ll own the work. Ask questions in the #tryout-<candidate> thread. We want to see your approach, not perfect polish."
- Daily standup (15–30m):
   - "What did you ship since yesterday? What’s blocked? Any infra/access needs?"
   - Mentor: unblock, not do the work. Point to internal docs, propose minor guardrails.
- Code review expectations: lightweight, focused on correctness and safety. Reserve heavy refactors for post-hire.
- Final demo prep: help candidate rehearse for 30min demo, prompt with likely panel questions.

Scoring rubric (observable signals, numeric 0–4 per dimension; pass threshold: average >= 3 and no critical fail):
- Technical correctness (0–4): does solution work and meet acceptance tests?
- System design & tradeoffs (0–4): shows reasoning, balances latency/cost/operability.
- Ownership & communication (0–4): clarity of commits, PR description, and demo narrative.
- Reliability & ops hygiene (0–4): tests, monitoring hooks, rollout plan.
- Collaborativeness (0–4): responds well to feedback, pairs comfortably.
- Culture-fit signal (0–4): values alignment, pragmatic judgement.
- Critical fails (free-text): security risk, integrity issues, inability to follow data handling rules. Any single marked critical fail requires escalation and likely rejection regardless of numeric score.

Conversion decision flow:
- Panel aggregation: each panelist submits numeric scores + top 3 evidence bullets. HR consolidates into a summary doc.
- Fast-fail window: if two or more reviewers mark candidate 0 or note a critical fail → fail.
- Borderline calibration: schedule 45m sync with hiring manager + 2 reviewers + People Ops to discuss. Possible outcomes: convert (offer), extend additional limited scope (extra 10–20h) to resolve targeted gaps, or decline.

Operational checklist (to be completed by People Ops + hiring manager):
[ ] Legal trial agreement signed (attach to candidate folder).
[ ] Dev sandbox and credentials provisioned (infra ticket: #).
[ ] Dedicated Slack channel created (#tryout-<name>).
[ ] Mentor assigned & paid mentoring buffer (2–4 hrs billed for mentoring time).
[ ] Acceptance tests and CI stubbed to run in sandbox.
[ ] Demo slot scheduled with panel (30–45m) + recording consent.
[ ] Conversion timeline & comms template drafted.

Templates (quick text snippets):
- Kickoff invite subject: "60hr Tryout — Kickoff: <candidate name> — <role>"
- Demo ask to panel: "Please review PR: <link> and score via form by EOD +2 days. Bring top 2 questions to the demo."
- Candidate closeout note (if converting): "Thanks — we’re excited to extend an offer. You’ll get formal comms from People Ops by <date>."

Open questions / risk log (items to resolve before org-wide usage):
- Legal: localized contractor vs. employee thresholds (need counsel for UK/DE/IN).
- Compensation: standardize band markup for trials that turn into offers; buffer for market hot skills.
- Accessibility: accommodate candidates who need longer timeframe or adjusted hours for disability — policy TBD.
- Ops: how to tag cloud cost for trial workloads (chargeback to hiring team).

Next steps (short term):
- Iterate this doc with hiring managers in Platform Eng + SRE (pilot 6 hires Q1).
- Create a public Confluence template with toggleable clauses for region/legal.
- Build a simple scoring Google Form to standardize panel inputs (owner: Maya).
- Run 1 cross-team calibration session after first 3 pilots.

Notes to self (Priya):
- Keep tasks small and real; avoid long-running epochs.
- Mentor training session: 30m pilot to align on "unblocked vs. solved" mentality.
- Slack channel naming convention: tryout-<candidate-lastname>-<role>.

References / precedents:
- Existing 72hr tryout docs (see: CONFLUENCE:HR/72hr-tryout) — lessons learned: candidate fatigue, unclear acceptance criteria.
- Hiring metrics to track: time-to-conversion, pass-rate, cost-per-successful-hire, candidate NPS.
